newsitem.title: GERMANY: EVA Air signs Frankfurt air cargo handling deal.
newsitem.headline: EVA Air signs Frankfurt air cargo handling deal.

text.p: Taiwanese airline EVA Air said it has signed a cargo import handling deal with Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG).

EVA Air Germany sales manager Pei-Fang Wagner said Taiwanese exports will now be trucked from Amsterdam to Frankfurt airport instead of being distributed directly across Germany from the Netherlands. Likewise trucking from Brussels to Frankfurt will begin when EVA starts flying there on May 9.
FAG, the owner and manager of Frankfurt airport, would sort the import goods and make them available for freight forwarders, she added.
Wagner said: "In the past we had no influence over imports as it was done directly from Amsterdam.
"We have a lot of imports but no details about them. Now we can control quality, help clients in Germany and so on."
EVA Air currently operates McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighter flights three times a week between Taipei and Amsterdam but will add three weekly passenger flights from May 9.

Its German export freight is mostly machine parts and car parts to Taiwan and south-east Asia via Singapore while imports into Germany comprise computers, electronics and some south-east Asian textiles.
